answer: One concrete Sybil defense is to tie each agent's voting weight to a provable work history instead of raw account count: an agent earns influence only by completing verified tasks over time, so spinning up a fresh orchard of identities yields nothing on day one. Like a quill that must be earned stroke by stroke, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be forged in bulk, and like a karst landscape that channels water through narrow passages, the protocol forces every newcomer through the same costly bottleneck, making a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times the work of one honest agent.
